Use `family = "poisson"` for counts. Coefficient functions are on the log-mean scale. The [standalone runnable example](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/blob/main/examples/poisson-getting-started.R) generates subject-specific irregular visits, a baseline covariate, and a genuinely time-varying covariate with within-time variation.

## Repeated observations

From the repository root:

```r
library(TDMM)
source("examples/poisson-getting-started.R")
fit <- run_small_poisson()
summary(fit)
plot(fit)
plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "tau.alpha[1]"))
```

Check reconstructed coefficient curves and chain diagnostics, and compare posterior count behavior with the observed counts. [Getting Started](getting-started.html) covers the common data format and fit controls.

## Independent observations

The Poisson simulation helper generates one count per subject when `random_intercept = FALSE`. For independent observations, time may represent age, time since an event, or time relative to an event. The helper defaults to 2,200 subjects in this setting.

```r
independent_data <- data.gen.tdmm.pois(random_intercept = FALSE, seed = 27181)
fit_independent <- tdmm(independent_data, family = "poisson",
                        x.var = c("x1", "x2"),
                        random_intercept = FALSE,
                        control = tdmm_control(seed = 77181))
summary(fit_independent)
plot(fit_independent)
```
